anika (Platform): Heads up — noticed a large number of traces for /v2/infer that only show ingress/router spans, missing the worker/gpu child spans since ~03:14 UTC. Any idea?
kevin (Telemetry): seeing the same in the per-route flamegraphs :eyes:. spike in partial traces starting 03:13:40 UTC, most show router -> ingress then stop.
matt (Runtime): did the routing-policy rollout finish around that time? I pushed a tweak to header canonicalization at 03:12.
deploy-bot: deploy canary routing-policy/v3 started by matt at 2026-05-18T03:12:10Z
huma (SRE): also saw a blip of exporter 429s reported by collector at 03:13. Not sure if related. envoys reported some header parsing warnings.
kevin (Telemetry): grabbed a raw request from the trace archive. headers look funky — tracestate appears before traceparent in the replay we saved. our collector parser currently assumes traceparent is first and bails if it can't find it in the first 16 headers. snippet:
```
POST /v2/infer HTTP/1.1
Host: api.redwood.local
tracestate: congo=BleGNlZQ,rojo=123
traceparent: 00-4bf92f3577b34da6a3ce929d0e0e4736-00f067aa0ba902b7-01
user-agent: curl/7.88.1
...
```
kevin (Telemetry): because we only search the first N headers for perf, if middleware reorders headers the collector misses traceparent entirely and emits an orphan root.
matt (Runtime): argh — that canonicalization change forces header sort by name to satisfy a downstream proxy. I didn't realize it would move tracestate above traceparent.
anika (Platform): can we make the collector tolerant (scan whole header list) as a quick mitigation? or do a rollback of the header reorder?
matt (Runtime): rolling back the header-ordering tweak now. rolling: canary -> off for v3.
deploy-bot: routing-policy/v3 rollback started by matt at 2026-05-18T03:21:03Z
huma (SRE): rollback completed at 03:25:12 UTC. I verified envoy logs — traceparent restored to expected position for most requests. :thumbsup:
kevin (Telemetry): after rollback I reprocessed the previously orphaned batch — child spans reattached. gap closed. saving the diff to s3://redwood-debug/traces/1717623456-orphans.diff
anika (Platform): thanks. two action items: (1) collector change to scan headers without strict positional assumptions + unit tests, (2) add a small e2e test that reorders tracestate/traceparent in the proxy integration.
matt (Runtime): agreed. I'll open a PR for the rollback fix and add a note to the rollout checklist about header ordering.
kevin (Telemetry): creating telemetry issue: RH-telemetry-482 "collector: tolerate out-of-order trace headers" and adding test cases.
huma (SRE): leaving a short incident note in #incidents with links to logs and the s3 dump.
anika (Platform): Great. Filing a post-incident doc and tagging runtime/telemetry. If anyone sees weird residuals ping here.
observability-bot: alert resolved for partial-traces-high in prod at 2026-05-18T03:27:10Z
anika (Platform): thanks all — nice catch + fast rollback. We'll track the follow-ups in RH-telemetry-482 and the rollout checklist update. :sparkles:
